---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify a Domainry backend from accepted requirements or delivered frontend evidence. Use for metadata-first Domainry projects, frontend-to-Runtime replacement, Runtime integration, and full-stack defect routing. Keeps frontend evidence read-only except an explicitly authorized Data Exchange offline-export center.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Each run owns one explicit Delivery Batch and follows exactly `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. A batch is an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Keep one project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`; copy [the template](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) only when it is absent, then resume its `Current stage`. Do not invent stages, state files, or continuation workflows.

The accepted product scope remains the baseline: never silently reduce it to an MVP. Put stable Requirement IDs and Feature keys in the current batch, record deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership, and include every shared resource or regression boundary affected by the batch. `done` means this batch is complete, not that deferred product scope was delivered.

Resolve this file's directory as `SKILL_ROOT` and set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`. Use only that packaged CLI. The five lifecycle commands are `model capability`, `model plan`, `apply model`, `apply finalize`, and `verify`; `project check` is their read-only pre-finalize source gate and never writes a receipt.

## requirements

Read [requirements and domain truth](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and the [PRD template](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Settle domain truth inside this stage for the current batch and its dependency closure: actors and scope; objects, relations, states, defaults, and retention; commands, transactions, idempotency, calculations, and external effects; Reports and offline export intent; schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. Classify time ownership explicitly: pausing one already-started Workflow execution until one due time is a Workflow `timer`/`wait_*` plus Runtime `record_timer`, while starting distinct runs for repeated calendar or interval windows is Scheduler recurrence. Never create a tenant Scheduler definition for a one-time continuation. `workspace` is Domainry's tenant boundary, not a peer of a separate tenant concept: translate tenant wording in requirements to workspace context, and never author a `tenant` or `workspace` Object/table, project-owned `tenant_id`/`workspace_id`, or duplicate workspace identity/projection. A company, customer, merchant, store, or other independently required business aggregate must use its actual domain name and lifecycle, never `tenant` as an infrastructure surrogate. Any required human approve/reject wait is a Runtime Workflow requirement, not two synchronous Handler branches. Any required downloadable Report export is a governed `report_export_controls` plus offline Data Exchange requirement, not a Report permission alone.

When frontend source exists, inspect it as evidence, including typed-client and raw HTTP call sites, query/mutation hooks, loaders, polling, API Mock adapters, handlers, fixtures, seeds, and mutation side effects. Keep the complete stable `FAPI-*` inventory and intent/read-composition grouping in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; use the current TODO as the per-batch audit queue that carries those same IDs through classification, contract closure, implementation, and verification. `frontend/**` is read-only except for the authorized export-center slice described below. Treat it as evidence, not authority for missing policy. Record frontend defects for owner `frontend`; do not hide them with backend workarounds. Preserve the accepted product baseline in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` and record a traceable current-batch delta with stable Requirement IDs, sources, owners, acceptance results, Feature ownership and deferred scope. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes current-batch observable behavior, authorization, money/units, an irreversible effect, or state flow.

When an admitted Project Builder demand declares `project_navigation`, the frontend compiler artifact named there is the complete menu-definition authority. Read it as immutable evidence and never reproduce, summarize, or edit its labels, routes, icons, parentage, or ordering. This backend stage owns only the mapping from published human Role keys to those compiled menu keys; there is one tenant-independent template and no application, client, surface, device, or end dimension.

## model

Select the one task profile and comma-separated requirement topics from the accepted current-batch dependency closure, then request one exact minimum reading plan. Use topic `delayed-continuation` for a one-time Workflow wait and `scheduler` only for true recurrence. Its `capability_contracts` is the complete inlined machine-contract closure for that scope; do not scan the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md) or issue one `model capability --key` call per category. Read every returned `read_order` path once, in order, relative to `SKILL_ROOT`. The returned documents, including [backend model](references/backend-model.md) when selected, remain authoritative—the plan removes discovery calls, not semantics. Preserve the complete current desired state in `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`; prefer one Feature per model file, and change only current-batch Features plus the declared shared-resource closure. Never edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**`, and never emit compiler-owned `capability_assembly`, standalone Permission definitions, versions, ownership, or seed metadata. Author each ordinary human Role directly as an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` grants; that shorthand expands to the published `any`/`manual`/workspace-provisioned defaults. In `project.initial_workspace_administrator_role`, explicitly select the one Role assigned to the first Workspace administrator; it must be workspace-provisioned, use `audience:any|user`, use `assignment_mode:manual`, and have no `required_binding_key`. Never infer this selection from a Role suffix, risk level, permissions, ordering, or the first Role. Use an extended Role with `audience: "service"` and `assignment_mode: "system_managed"` for an internal Workflow/Scheduler execution identity, and omit `provision_to_workspaces` (preferred) or set it to false; bind that Role by key through Workflow `run_as`, including a Workflow targeted by Scheduler. Never convert an internal role into a human tenant-login actor to satisfy validation.

Classify every writable Object as either plain `direct_crud`, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or cross-record command. Do not author new Automation. A human approval must be an enabled Workflow graph with an approval task, authorized assignee resolver, explicit approved and rejected branches, and terminal Action effects; standalone approve/reject Handlers are not the waiting process. Reports use `object_sql_v1`; inside its SQL, wrap every model-derived Object and field identifier in MySQL backticks even when the key is not a SQL keyword, while keeping aliases, parameter names, and result aliases unquoted. A bounded same-Object aggregate across Runtime-installed Workspaces uses the separate `cross-workspace-aggregate` topic and never caller SQL or Workspace IDs. Use `organization-delivery` for Runtime-selected ownership targets and store provisioning, `identity-handler-delivery` for atomic Identity/Profile delivery, and `workspace-identity-usage` for installation-authorized account counts. Every required export also authors the Blueprint `report_export_controls` closure (bounded rows, audit/download Objects and mappings, requester-owned grants, assurance/masking when required) while Runtime Report and Data Exchange own execution.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --reading-profile <initial-delivery|feature-increment|handler-repair> \
  --topics <records,permissions,identity-profile,identity-handler-delivery,organization,organization-delivery,reporting-line,workflow,delayed-continuation,scheduler,reports,report-export,cross-workspace-aggregate,workspace-identity-usage,notifications,connectors,agents,entrypoints,workspace-provisioning,files,domain-truth>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model plan` performs one immutable load of the complete current model, validates the whole cross-resource draft, derives capability and authorization closure, persists deterministic diagnostics/provenance, and reports the Ledger change set. On failure, repair the complete stdout `diagnostics` batch using each file/JSON Pointer, constraint, actual/allowed value and hint before rerunning; its `artifact` path, relative to `--project`, retains the full provenance. Use only the exact contract keys returned in `capability_contracts`; Runtime execution-only modules have none. A Delivery Batch is not a loader or apply filter. Confirm that every create, update and delete belongs to the batch or its declared impact closure; repair the named owner and rerun. Once valid, keep the model unchanged while reviewing removals and evolution-sensitive changes.

## apply

Read [project mutation](references/project-mutation.md), then apply the reviewed model:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module>
```

Gate on the returned state before reading or writing implementation source. `implementation_ready` or `applied` is materialized success. `evolution_review_required` is an exit-0, non-terminal control state with `materialization_state:not_materialized`: inspect the exact immutable `evolution_audit_path`; verify its raw bytes with `evolution_audit_file_sha256` and `evolution_audit_file_size_bytes`, for example `test "$(shasum -a 256 "$PROJECT_ROOT/$evolution_audit_path" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$evolution_audit_file_sha256" && test "$(wc -c < "$PROJECT_ROOT/$evolution_audit_path" | tr -d '[:space:]')" = "$evolution_audit_file_size_bytes"`; and confirm the JSON document's `audit_sha256` equals `evolution_audit_sha256`. `evolution_audit_sha256_kind:canonical_semantic_identity` means this latter value is the canonical semantic identity computed with the self-hash field empty, not the raw file digest, and it is the value embedded in `next_command`; never compare it to raw `shasum` output. Then rerun the returned `next_command` after replacing its reason placeholder with a non-empty explanation of the reviewed diff. Do not continue to source implementation or finalization until that reapply returns `implementation_ready` or `applied`; repair revalidates the canonical audit content and current inputs, so a tampered or stale audit, omitted SHA/reason, or failed repair remains a non-zero failure. On successful reapply, `evolution_source_finalization.state:deferred_unfinalized_source` means the audit proved the previous delivery had never been finalized: the reviewed in-progress source was preserved, not trusted or finalized, and the ordinary focused-test/`apply finalize` gate remains mandatory. Never delete an existing finalization receipt to force this state; its file SHA is bound into the audit.

If the admitted demand names a compiled navigation artifact, create or update exactly one project-owned `backend/config/navigation-role-menus.json` before finalization. Its only schema is `{"contract_version":"domainry-project-role-menu-sets-v1","role_menu_sets":[{"role_key":"<published-human-role>","menu_keys":["<compiled-menu-key>"]}]}`. Use only workspace-provisioned human Roles from the current model and menu keys present in the compiler artifact. Do not add menu definitions, tenant/workspace IDs, permissions, routes, presentation fields, or client/end selectors. Do not create this file when no compiled navigation artifact exists. Finalization verifies the compiler source digest and menu-key closure and generates the Runtime bootstrap template; Runtime validates the published Role closure, and Identity copies the template into each new Workspace exactly once.

Retain the immutable implementation packet only from a materialized-success response. Read the compact packet index once: its `actions` array is the complete exact Action-context path list, `summary.shared_constraints` applies to every Action, and `summary.test_commands` is the copyable command contract for this delivery. Read its exact `verification.path` core during apply—not after finalization—then read each shard in `verification.minimum_read_plan` exactly once after checking its published byte count and SHA-256; those shards contain only the listed `route_keys` reachable from this project's compiled manifest. Never enumerate or read unlisted route artifacts, and never read the full source route catalog—the core's `route_catalog` identity preserves its completeness. Before authoring any business-flow source, consume `evidence_contract` as the complete marker grammar: use its allowed `source` values and numeric `requirement_id_pattern`, and implement every flow-specific `required_operations` entry with its exact source and `required_observations` (BF08 publishes all seven governed-export steps). Copy `verification.harness_template.path` verbatim to `backend/tests/businessflow/harness_test.go` and author scenarios rather than regenerating transport, authentication, response-decoding, and evidence infrastructure. Consume `setup_contract`, compact `routes`, and the focused shards directly. Build every business-flow precondition for an `action_only` Object through a published authored Action; when a flow needs business actors or organizations, use an authored Identity HandlerDelivery or OrganizationDelivery Action. Bootstrap materializes the Blueprint's eligible human Workspace Roles, assigns only the explicitly selected `initial_workspace_administrator_role` to the first administrator, and keeps service/system-managed Roles out of tenant login provisioning. If the authored Action surface cannot establish an exact required state, repair the Blueprint and Handler contract before finalization, rerun `model plan`, then follow `setup_contract.post_apply_repair`; never inject records, roles, users, organizations, or historical timestamps through a startup fixture. Then read each compact Action context by exact path and follow that context's `read_order` once, in order, relative to `PROJECT_ROOT/backend`; those exact generated contracts and project-owned source/test files replace embedded source dumps and broad generated-tree scans. For this packet, implement only the project-owned backend source and paired tests, and create every required `backend/tests/businessflow` case for this batch. Consume every call outcome in Handler and helper source: never use `_` to discard all returns or an error/`ok` result from a capability, method, constructor, parser, or local helper. A data result may be ignored only while its sibling error is bound and handled, such as `_, err := caps.Store.Update(...)`; `value, _ := parse(...)`, `_, _ = call(...)`, and `_ = call(...)` are forbidden. Every multi-item command or query uses one generated batch/bulk capability call; never loop over a single-item capability or Runtime API to simulate batch behavior, including through helper indirection. Pure in-memory loops are allowed only when needed to build bounded batch inputs or correlate results and must contain no capability I/O. If the required true-batch primitive is absent, repair the owning contract instead of hiding the gap with pseudo-batch code; use a bounded sequential fallback only when true batch cannot be implemented and the accepted requirement explicitly defines its non-atomic, partial-failure semantics. For a selected custom Connector, request its focused context with `model capability --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementation. Never edit generated source, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or managed Runtime state.

Apply the batch rule according to execution shape. One accepted user write intent maps to one Runtime command; its Handler completes every required create, update, delete, derived state, audit, and durable intent atomically inside the same Runtime-owned UoW, or rolls the whole intent back. Reads need not share a transaction unless the accepted requirement explicitly needs one point-in-time invariant. For a list page, load only the bounded page, collect its distinct relation IDs, resolve each relation set with one generated batch query, and correlate the results in memory; for example, a customer page resolves all displayed salesperson names from that page's salesperson IDs in one batch, never one query per customer. Do not prefetch later pages or merge unrelated domains into one snapshot merely to save a request. Statistical and Report results must use Object SQL or a published backend aggregate capability; never manufacture multiple pages in Go or a frontend, fetch Shift, settlement, or other fact rows into memory, and aggregate them there. The bounded sequential fallback above applies only to an accepted sequence of independent intents, never to one write intent, page relation enrichment, or Report/statistical aggregation.

The only frontend mutation exception is a Data Exchange offline-export center for an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; follow [its contract](references/frontend-offline-report-export.md). Otherwise report the owner gap.

Follow `summary.stage_boundary` literally: finish all project-owned source, then run `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile` before finalization; `focused` runs the Action tests and then `project check`, the exact read-only project-source validation also used by finalization. Treat either part as the same focused gate and repair every emitted diagnostic before advancing. A full-tree failure caused by not-yet-generated composition is not an implementation failure. The shared harness is a template copied into project-owned tests, never imported from `.domainry`. After both pre-finalize commands pass run `summary.test_commands.finalize`, then and only then run `summary.test_commands.full_tree`. These commands already contain the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, and project-local-plus-public hybrid `GOPROXY`; do not replace them with a default or local-only proxy. Once finalization succeeds, project-owned source is frozen for this verification attempt. Any later source change starts a new repair iteration and requires the focused/compile/finalize sequence again; do not continue the stale attempt into `verify`.

Finalize every delivered Handler and Connector:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`apply finalize` enforces source call-site contracts, including consumed call outcomes, guarded `ConditionalUpdate`, and the no-pseudo-batch invariant across capability aliases, callbacks, and named local helper call chains. `project check` calls that exact validation without resolving finalization dependencies or writing a receipt; use only the packet-provided command and do not add manual grep gates. Run the affected backend test set before advancing.

## verify

Read [evidence levels](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification](references/verification.md), and [Runtime integration](references/backend-runtime.md). The implementation packet's verification guide and every required business-flow test must already have been consumed/completed during apply. Verify is read-and-run only: do not create, edit, rename, or delete project-owned source after finalization. Every current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary needs a complete project-owned case with explicit preconditions, ordered actions, and a terminal durable result; denial cases also prove unchanged state. For every module HTTP step, resolve the exact route in the implementation packet and grant that route's `authorization.permission` with its `required_role_grant.data_scope` to the selected actor Role before finalization; Report audience/source data access never substitutes for the executable route Permission. Decode Runtime record pages only as top-level `items`, with business fields in each `items[].data` and record metadata such as `id`/`updated_at` on the item envelope. Unchanged flows may reuse only current baseline evidence. Run the highest-risk changed case against the managed Runtime before broader flow verification.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` reuses structural/package receipts only after their complete source, model, Runtime and dependency identities validate; otherwise it runs the complete backend tree and rebuilds. It always proves healthy start and same-cohort restart, then leaves Runtime stopped and emits stage/cache telemetry. `backend/tests/businessflow` is a black-box Runtime package: it may use published Runtime HTTP/client operations but never import project Handlers, generated capability/data fakes, or database drivers. For both phases every BF01-BF08 test emits its structured evidence marker exactly as verification documents. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. A shared login, health, read, or Action-catalog probe does not prove another named flow; each claimed Runtime case must execute its own ordered Runtime journey and read back its terminal durable result. Approval cases start the Workflow, observe the task, prove unauthorized denial, decide both branches, and read back process/task/business state. Export cases query and prepare the governed Report export, follow the requester-owned Data Exchange job to completion/download, and prove another actor is denied. Verify only requirement-observable denial, scope, conflict, rollback, replay, restart, worker, Report, export, file, notification, and provider behavior. Do not create a project evidence ledger or generic acceptance runner.

## done

Set `Current stage: done` only when every current-batch finding is resolved and current receipts, tests, durable observations, and Runtime identity support the claim. Report batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations without claiming deferred product work is complete.

Project-owned edits are limited to requirements/TODO evidence, declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, and the authorized export-center exception. Recoverable failures stay in the current stage: repair the responsible owner and rerun the same direct command.
# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Build one canonical frontend backend-interaction inventory in the PRD before capability discovery. Search typed-client calls, direct `fetch`/HTTP clients, query and mutation hooks, route loaders, polling, download/export calls, Mock adapters/handlers, tests, and any helper that can hide a request. Give each unique interaction shape a stable `FAPI-*` ID, cite every call site that uses it, and assign an `INTENT-*` group for a user-visible write intent or a `READ-*` group for one read composition. Multiple call sites may share one `FAPI-*` row only when their operation, request shape, business meaning, and execution rule are the same; the row's evidence still lists all call sites. Pure router, local-storage, and presentation behavior is recorded as `frontend_only`, not invented as a backend dependency.

For an initial backend, complete frontend replacement, or unbaselined project, inventory every backend-bound frontend interaction. For an increment or repair with an accepted inventory baseline, carry only current-batch, dependency-closure, and affected-regression `FAPI-*` rows into the TODO and cite the immutable baseline for unchanged rows. The PRD remains the complete fact source; the TODO is the transient per-batch work queue and must not become a second independently maintained interface specification. Reconcile counts for discovered call sites, inventoried `FAPI-*` rows, intent/read groups, dispositioned rows, rule-adjudicated groups, and unresolved findings.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

Classify each `INTENT-*` or `READ-*` group by execution shape before capability discovery: `write_intent`, `page_list`, `page_relation_batch`, `detail_read`, `independent_read`, or `report_statistic`. One accepted user write intent has one Runtime command and one atomic Runtime-owned UoW covering all required creates, updates, deletes, derived state, audit, and durable intents; judge the whole ordered request sequence, not each mutation in isolation. A read may span independent bounded queries unless the accepted business invariant explicitly requires one point-in-time snapshot. A list requirement records its page bound and every displayed relation enrichment: collect the current page's distinct relation IDs and resolve each relation set with one batch query, never one query per row. A statistical or Report requirement names Object SQL or a published backend aggregate as its calculation owner; fetching multiple pages of Shift, settlement, payroll, or other fact rows into frontend or Go memory and aggregating them there is not an acceptable implementation. Do not place unrelated domains in one consistency snapshot merely to reduce request count; share a snapshot only when a named business invariant requires those facts to be observed together.

Record one rule verdict for the whole group as `compliant`, `backend_contract_gap`, `backend_implementation_gap`, `frontend_integration_gap`, `platform_gap`, `frontend_only`, `superseded`, or `open`. Frontend evidence proves the actor trigger and current request sequence; it cannot by itself prove a Runtime UoW, Handler implementation, SQL aggregation, or durable rollback. Carry every applicable `FAPI-*` and group ID through the TODO stages: requirements closes inventory and adjudication, model closes the required Runtime contract, apply closes implementation, and verify closes current evidence. Do not leave requirements merely because files were searched while an in-scope row remains undiscovered, ungrouped, or unadjudicated.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

The Report source of truth performs its filtering, grouping, and aggregation in backend Object SQL or a published aggregate capability. Pagination is a delivery bound, not an aggregation algorithm: never plan a frontend or Handler loop that preconstructs or walks pages, accumulates all fact rows, and computes the Report in memory.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

# Project-owned source

Git owns project source. Edit, format, test, rename, and delete in-scope project source with normal development tools while preserving unrelated work. Treat a canonical Handler and its paired test as one review unit and keep both aligned with the same implementation-packet entry. `frontend/**` remains read-only except when an exportable Object SQL Report requires the Data Exchange export center and the TODO says `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; evidence that assigns any other defect to the frontend produces a finding with owner `frontend`, never an edit.

Allowed backend source includes `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum`, `backend/actions/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. The sole frontend allowance is the existing project's route/navigation, feature components, typed-client integration, localization, and focused tests needed for the export center in [offline Report export frontend](frontend-offline-report-export.md); do not mutate unrelated frontend source. Never edit `backend/generated/**`, `backend/cmd/**`, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, caches, journals, packages, or other `.domainry/**` state. The only writable `.domainry` exception is the current session's `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` TODO.

## Normal delivered-batch sequence

This is the only source sequence after `apply model` returns `implementation_ready` or `applied`. An exit-0 `evolution_review_required` response with `materialization_state:not_materialized` is not this boundary: inspect its immutable audit path/SHA, review the exact diff, rerun its `next_command` with the exact SHA and a non-empty reason, and gate again on the returned state. Missing review flags, a stale audit, and a failed evolution remain non-zero. Never read an old packet or continue implementation/finalization from the review-required state. A ready response may report `evolution_source_finalization.state:deferred_unfinalized_source` only for audit-proven never-finalized source; preserve and complete that source, but do not treat it as trusted—the ordinary focused tests and `apply finalize` remain mandatory.

1. Retain the exact `.implementation_packet.path`, delivery/materialization identity, file hash, returned `actions[]` direct-path index, `summary`, and `verification` reference from `apply model`. That command validates every delivered Action context, creates only missing canonical Handler/test skeletons, and persists immutable content-addressed context files under managed `.domainry/builder/**`.
2. Read the packet index once. Apply `summary.shared_constraints` to the whole batch, then for one Action at a time find its exact `action_key` and read that entry's `path` directly. The file is already the complete single-Action context, including only its referenced document content; do not run `jq`, reconstruct a document table, use `latest.json`, or read generated capabilities/context files directly.
3. Implement the complete Action-context Handler and paired test directly with normal source-editing tools. If either file changed concurrently, stop and reconcile both against the immutable context before continuing.
4. For an approved Connector source gap, load `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project <project> --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementing that Connector under `backend/connectors/**`. Action packet context does not replace Connector context.

Read the `verification.path` core, consume its complete `evidence_contract` and `setup_contract`, verify and read each listed `verification.minimum_read_plan` shard, copy `verification.harness_template.path` verbatim to `backend/tests/businessflow/harness_test.go`, and implement every required black-box case under `backend/tests/businessflow` before finalization. If test design proves the authored Action surface is insufficient, return to the Blueprint, run `model plan`, and follow `setup_contract.post_apply_repair` through audit review and reapply before resuming source work. Do not regenerate the shared transport/auth/fixture/evidence helpers. Implement other allowed project-owned backend source/tests and the authorized export-center exception. Never discard all call returns or any error/`ok` result in Handler or helper source; bind and handle it. Run the exact `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile`; they already carry the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, focused packages, project-local-plus-public hybrid proxy, and the finalizer's same-source read-only project check after focused Go tests.

Never use the full tree before finalization because the generated composition is intentionally incomplete at that stage. After successful finalization, freeze project-owned source for the verification attempt. Any source change starts a new repair iteration and requires focused tests, business-flow compile, and finalization again; never run `verify` against a stale receipt.

There is no second prepare, per-Action context, or source-write command.

The batch-prepared skeleton compiles against delivered capability types but intentionally returns `*.not_implemented`. It exposes missing implementation coverage and is never positive-path evidence. Replace the paired generated test's nil Execution call and placeholder oracle with typed non-nil Execution/capability stubs and assertions over current outputs and business effects; a generic no-panic assertion is not meaningful behavior evidence.

## Finalization boundary

After source/tests are implemented and every preceding implementation TODO item is closed, follow the packet's three command boundary without editing it. Finalization scans delivery-bound canonical Action source/test paths. A Handler paired with a generated test that still has nil Execution or an exact `*.not_implemented` oracle returns `state:"invalid"`; source-policy and applicable Go compile failures also fail closed. Finalize writes only its failure receipt on failure. Cross-module/full verification, packaging, and Runtime start require the current successful finalization. For business-flow work, the immutable `verification.path` core, its verified `minimum_read_plan` shards, and copied harness template replace repository or archive search and preserve the black-box boundary.
# Project source ownership and extensions

This Skill owns backend modeling and the in-scope project source integration. Frontend evidence is read-only during requirements. The only frontend implementation exception is the Data Exchange export center required by an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; every other defect assigned to `frontend/**` becomes a finding (owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, contract basis), and a truly blocked journey is marked blocked.

`backend/model/*.json` is the only metadata authoring surface. `apply model` owns Ledger convergence, validation, publication, and backend materialization. `apply finalize` owns source validation and the finalization receipt after implementation.

Use Runtime metadata for schema, plain CRUD, state-machine invariants, Workflow, Scheduler, Reports, and published Connector operations. Any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or multi-record write is project-owned source behind a Handler Action; its written Objects are `action_only`. Automation and system Actions are not new behavior-authoring choices.

Project-owned source this Skill edits normally lives under `backend/actions/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. For the authorized export-center exception, edit only the existing frontend route/navigation, feature components, typed Runtime Client integration, localization, and focused tests described in [offline Report export frontend](frontend-offline-report-export.md). Generated backend source, Runtime manifests, materialization state, receipts, caches, and `.domainry/**` are never edited by this Skill.

For a suspected frontend defect, compare the explicit requirement, typed API, Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never use a frontend adapter or fallback expectation to hide it. Record the frontend-owned defect as a finding with minimal reproduction and contract basis instead of repairing it.

Each Action or Connector belongs to one model module. Keep source under that module's generated layout, use the bounded context from the single packaged CLI, and do not duplicate an implementation for different consumers.

System configuration defaults remain Runtime-owned. Project overrides may use `backend/config/runtime.json` only for published non-secret keys; deployment and secret sources retain higher precedence.
# Behavior ownership

Behavior tuples are compiler output, not backend-model input. Model only the
business resource and, for a project-owned Handler, the reason plain CRUD is
insufficient:

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "item.submit": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "The item update and submission receipt must commit atomically",
        "access": {
          "item": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "item_submission": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Plane derives the complete Ledger behavior from the resource:

| Resource | Derived owner | Derived shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object not written by a Handler | `runtime_crud` | `record_write / single_record / single_record / reject_write` |
| Action without Handler | `runtime_system_action` | `business_command / single_record / single_record / rollback_command` |
| Action with Handler | `business_handler` | single- or multi-record from the access union, with rollback |
| before Automation | `automation_before` | before persistence, reject write |
| after Automation | `automation_after` | after commit, eventual, preserve committed write |
| Workflow | `workflow` | process / long-running / resume |
| Scheduled Job | `scheduler` | schedule / long-running / retry |

For a Handler, read operations are `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`,
`exists`, and `count`; write operations are `create`, `update`,
`conditional_update`, `delete`, and `restore`. Plane sorts those Object sets,
uses their union as `involved_objects`, chooses single- versus multi-record
scope, copies `handler.reason` into rationale/capability gap, and emits the
host-owned transaction/rollback requirement.

The Feature owns traceability. Every resource inherits its enclosing Feature
requirement unless it explicitly supplies a non-empty `requirements` override.
Plane emits the same derived behavior into every linked requirement. A Feature
with no Object CRUD, Action, Automation, Workflow, or Scheduled Job receives a
compiler-generated no-executable reason.

Do not author `behaviors`, `owner`, `resource_key`, `read_set`, `write_set`,
`involved_objects`, `atomicity`, `failure_semantics`, `transaction_requirement`,
or Ledger dependencies. The internal Ledger retains and validates all of them.

Write ownership is also derived. A Handler-written Object is `action_only`; an
otherwise writable Object is `direct_crud`. Direct CRUD permissions or
entrypoint mutation exposure on a Handler-written Object fail
`model.write_ownership_conflict` before Ledger generation.
# Verification evidence levels

Read this contract during model/apply and before authoring `backend/tests/businessflow`; do not defer it until verify after project-owned source is frozen. The implementation packet's `evidence_contract` is the machine-readable marker grammar and flow-specific required-operation projection of these semantics.

Use this ladder for every verification check and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, and packaging pass through `verify`. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope business-flow case executes end to end on real Runtime data. Each case starts from explicit preconditions, performs the ordered business actions, and observes its terminal durable result; requirement-defined denial, scope and failure branches are included.
- `L4_browser_verified`: reserved for the authorized offline export center when the project already provides a supported local browser verification path. Other browser-layer UI verification remains outside this Skill.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every business-flow case, bind project-local evidence to the current source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record its requirement/flow ID, test name/path, actor/role, ordered actions, permission and data scope, persistence probe, terminal result, and audit/receipt identity when applicable.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

A Delivery Batch requires current L3 for every in-scope business flow and L5 for every changed or affected critical flow marked restart-sensitive. Unchanged flows may reference prior evidence only when it is still bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity; every changed flow and affected regression boundary must reach the same level in the current batch. Whole-product completion may be claimed only when no Requirement ID remains deferred. When the authorized offline export center changes frontend source, its focused tests and smallest relevant build/typecheck are mandatory; reach L4 only when the project already provides a supported local browser path. Other frontend-owned defects remain findings for the frontend owner.

## One verification model

Verification uses project-owned business-flow test cases and one CLI-owned,
temporary evidence protocol. There is no acceptance denominator, generic case runner,
carry-forward/stale-report workflow, or project-owned second evidence ledger.

Each current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary has one stable flow ID and one or more ordinary project-owned test cases under `backend/**`. Group cross-module cases under `backend/tests/businessflow/` when that makes ownership clearer; keep focused unit cases beside their source. A flow case starts from explicit preconditions, uses the requirement's real actor and scope, performs the ordered business actions, and asserts the terminal business result through durable read-back. It is not a list of disconnected endpoint checks. An unchanged flow may reuse prior evidence only when the TODO identifies that evidence and proves it remains bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity.

When frontend evidence exists, reconcile the TODO with the PRD's canonical `FAPI-*` inventory before completion. Every selected `FAPI-*` row belongs to one `INTENT-*` or `READ-*` group and reaches a terminal disposition; discovered call-site, inventory-row, group, adjudication, and unresolved-finding totals must balance for the selected audit scope. Verify the complete group rather than treating each endpoint as an independent success: a write group proves one Runtime command plus rollback and replay semantics, a page-list group preserves its bound and batch relation lookups, and a Report/statistical group proves backend SQL or aggregate ownership. Frontend source evidence alone never proves the Handler UoW or aggregate implementation. One business-flow case may close several member `FAPI-*` rows when it executes their accepted journey and records their stable IDs in TODO evidence.

The current-batch business-flow inventory and affected regression closure must cover:

- every current-batch happy path from initial state through all required transitions to its terminal observable result;
- every requirement-defined alternate or rejection branch, including authorization, data-scope, validation and conflict behavior;
- unchanged durable state after a denied, invalid or failed action;
- idempotent replay, transaction rollback, concurrency, restart/resume, notification, schedule, file, integration, Object SQL Report, offline export submission, actor-owned job-list visibility or completed download only when the accepted flow actually depends on it;
- current-batch Requirement ID → Feature key → flow ID → test name/path traceability, plus baseline references for unchanged affected flows.

Do not multiply cases for platform internals that no business requirement observes. One flow case may prove several operations when they are steps of the same business journey. Conversely, do not call a set of isolated unit tests complete when no case executes the required journey end to end.

## Terminal state

`done` requires all current-batch business flows and affected regression boundaries to have current passing cases, the highest-risk changed real Runtime flow to pass, structural verification and package receipts to be current, and the batch finding inventory to be empty. It closes only the Delivery Batch; whole-product completion additionally requires an empty deferred Requirement inventory. A genuinely unavailable external provider may be reported as `verification_blocked` only after every authorized local or sandbox route is exhausted; an ordinary failed case remains a repair finding. Successful CLI verification ends in `verified_and_stopped` with no managed Runtime intentionally left running.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`. Change it to `done` only after the policy above is satisfied and the TODO evidence points to current CLI receipts and Runtime observations.

When the authorized offline export center is in scope, verification also runs its focused frontend tests and smallest relevant build/typecheck, and uses the project's supported browser verification path when available. Prove loading, empty, active, completed/downloadable, failed, cancelled, expired/denied, and cross-actor isolation states without treating a queued job as terminal. If the typed Data Exchange job-list operation is absent, keep the slice incomplete as an owner gap rather than substituting browser memory.

The final summary states the Delivery Batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, current-batch and affected-regression test results, managed Runtime result, focused export-center frontend result when applicable, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations. Unrelated browser-layer UI verification remains outside this Skill.

## One-time delayed continuation

Use `timer`, `wait_until`, or `wait_duration` when one already-started Workflow
must pause once and later continue as the same process. Runtime persists this
wait in the `record_timer` system Object; the global Record Timer worker claims
the row with fencing after `due_at` and resumes the ordinary Workflow path. Do
not add `scheduled_jobs` for this shape. Scheduler is for recurrence that starts
a distinct run for every calendar or interval window.

- `wait_duration` uses `contract.timer.duration_seconds` with a positive number.
- `wait_until` uses one RFC3339 `contract.timer.at` instant.
- `timer` uses `contract.timer.timer_key`, `purpose`, and either a positive
  duration, one RFC3339 `at`, or a date/datetime `source_field` from every
  trigger Object.

When an Action already calculates the exact business due instant, persist it in
a date/datetime field and point `contract.timer.source_field` at that
field. Do not also author `offset_seconds` or `business_calendar_key`: the timer
must consume the final instant, not recalculate calendar policy. A re-arming
Workflow uses `trigger_contract.type: field_changed` with that same
`field_key`; entry/continuation Actions set the next exact instant and exit or
cancel Actions clear it. The due Action re-reads the governing state and returns
an idempotent no-effect result for a stale timer before attempting mutations.

Verification reads the persisted `record_timer.due_at`, proves the downstream
Action and business effect are absent before `due_at`, then proves that after
the due instant the same Workflow process advances through the ordinary
claim/fencing/resume path. Use a short real future due and bounded polling only
when the accepted business surface already permits that value. Otherwise keep
the real business due: prove its calculation and persistence through the
production Action, prove the pre-due/due business branches in focused Handler
tests with a dependency-injected clock, and consume an independently produced
Runtime timer integration certificate for pre-due/due/restart mechanics. The
compiled manifest and immutable implementation packet bind those exact evidence
identities. Do not add a verification-only business Action/Workflow, expose a
clock or time field through production input, add a Runtime clock seam, or claim
a timer certificate that was not produced and identity-checked.

Approval outputs are process-wide bindings: use
`$workflow.approval_decision` and `$workflow.approval_comment` on terminal
branches. A node-local guess such as `$manager_approval.comment` or
`$director_approval.comment` is not a published binding and fails validation.

When a requirement says a person approves or rejects after waiting, the approval
node and its durable Runtime task are mandatory. Separate synchronous approve/reject Handlers,
a pending Object, or `approval_required` metadata alone cannot
replace the Workflow; terminal branch nodes may invoke the existing atomic
Handlers for their business effects.

Acceptance proves resolved assignees, unauthorized decision denial, each
terminal branch, durable process/task state, Handler business effects, retry and
restart resume. Do not replace an expressible graph with one giant Handler or
invent approval tokens and private workflow endpoints.

## One verification model

Verification uses project-owned business-flow test cases and one CLI-owned,
temporary evidence protocol. There is no acceptance denominator, generic case runner,
carry-forward/stale-report workflow, or project-owned second evidence ledger.

Each current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary has one stable flow ID and one or more ordinary project-owned test cases under `backend/**`. Group cross-module cases under `backend/tests/businessflow/` when that makes ownership clearer; keep focused unit cases beside their source. A flow case starts from explicit preconditions, uses the requirement's real actor and scope, performs the ordered business actions, and asserts the terminal business result through durable read-back. It is not a list of disconnected endpoint checks. An unchanged flow may reuse prior evidence only when the TODO identifies that evidence and proves it remains bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity.

When frontend evidence exists, reconcile the TODO with the PRD's canonical `FAPI-*` inventory before completion. Every selected `FAPI-*` row belongs to one `INTENT-*` or `READ-*` group and reaches a terminal disposition; discovered call-site, inventory-row, group, adjudication, and unresolved-finding totals must balance for the selected audit scope. Verify the complete group rather than treating each endpoint as an independent success: a write group proves one Runtime command plus rollback and replay semantics, a page-list group preserves its bound and batch relation lookups, and a Report/statistical group proves backend SQL or aggregate ownership. Frontend source evidence alone never proves the Handler UoW or aggregate implementation. One business-flow case may close several member `FAPI-*` rows when it executes their accepted journey and records their stable IDs in TODO evidence.

The current-batch business-flow inventory and affected regression closure must cover:

- every current-batch happy path from initial state through all required transitions to its terminal observable result;
- every requirement-defined alternate or rejection branch, including authorization, data-scope, validation and conflict behavior;
- unchanged durable state after a denied, invalid or failed action;
- idempotent replay, transaction rollback, concurrency, restart/resume, notification, schedule, file, integration, Object SQL Report, offline export submission, actor-owned job-list visibility or completed download only when the accepted flow actually depends on it;
- current-batch Requirement ID → Feature key → flow ID → test name/path traceability, plus baseline references for unchanged affected flows.

Do not multiply cases for platform internals that no business requirement observes. One flow case may prove several operations when they are steps of the same business journey. Conversely, do not call a set of isolated unit tests complete when no case executes the required journey end to end.

# Domain truth and settlement

## Requirement boundary

Freeze business facts before capability discovery. Platform capabilities decide how accepted facts map to Runtime; they do not decide what the facts are.

| Kind | Meaning | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Occurred fact | A completed business event and its event-time inputs, rules, and result | Persist when it occurs; correct by reversal or adjustment |
| Summary | A read-only aggregation of occurred facts | Use Object SQL; never own the formula that created the fact |
| Simulation | A hypothetical result under assumed inputs or rules | Isolate from official facts, ledgers, payroll, and reports |

For every material calculation, decide: Calculation Owner, Evaluation Time, Persisted Result, Policy/Rule Snapshot, Input Snapshot, Calculation Trace, Correction/Reversal Strategy, Downstream Consumers, and Report Source of Truth. Keep only the smallest affected modeling slice blocked when accepted evidence leaves at least two incompatible choices that change the explicitly required formula, amount/unit semantics, occurred-fact identity, correction behavior, or observable result. Exact decimal representation, a stated threshold, and summation remain modelable when optional currency, unit, or range metadata is absent; use nullable metadata and stated command preconditions, and do not invent conversion rules. Route Runtime-owned representations through contract discovery and reversible persistence, index, audit, idempotency, and concurrency mechanics through the `safe_implementation_decision` rule in [requirements-and-domain-truth.md](requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity); those choices do not become product business ambiguity, but their later verification remains mandatory.

## Versioned settlement pattern

```text
Versioned Policy
  → Atomic Settlement Action
  → Calculation Snapshot
  → Immutable Ledger
  → Reversal / Adjustment
  → Object SQL Report
  → Offline Data Exchange Export
  → Payroll / Export Reconciliation
```

Use this pattern for an event that locks money, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll input. In one transaction, the settlement Action must validate idempotency and authorization, resolve the event-time policy, and persist policy identity/version, the actual rule snapshot, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, final result, immutable ledger entries, and audit/outbox effects. A later policy version affects only later events.

Never update or delete an original financial ledger entry to correct history. Append a linked reversal for cancellation/refund and a reasoned adjustment for an approved correction. Preserve `reversal_of` or equivalent lineage, the original ledger ID, actor, time, reason, and approval boundary. A locked payroll/export consumer records the ledger IDs or a governed scope/hash it consumed; later adjustments follow the explicit correction period instead of silently changing the locked result.

## Anti-patterns

- Repeating one formula across pages or several reports.
- Joining current Settings to recompute a historical financial result.
- Rendering absent or unproven facts as numeric zero.
- Giving summary, detail, page, payroll, and export different scopes or formulas.
- Allowing Settings changes to drift historical results.
- Omitting ledger-ID-level traceability across consumers.
- Building a project-specific report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator.
- Authoring Runtime Report transport or export-execution internals in the project model.
- Using a second export-only query, a synchronous browser export, or treating Runtime mechanics as domain facts.
- Synthesizing an export-job list from browser memory or internal Data Exchange tables.

## Acceptance matrix

Cover applicable boundaries with event-time input, policy identity, snapshot/ledger IDs, trace, consumer result, and allow/deny evidence:

- policy version switch before/after effective time;
- business-day cutoff and cross-midnight events;
- multi-party allocation with deterministic remainder handling;
- full/partial refund and reversal lineage;
- correction after payroll or another consumer is locked;
- summary/detail/page/payroll/export reconciliation by ledger ID;
- cross-store and cross-entity permission/data-scope denial;
- Runtime restart and Settings change without historical drift.
- Object SQL result correctness, parameter semantics, and source-of-truth reconciliation;
- actor-owned offline export submission, export-center visibility, completed download, and cross-actor denial when export is required;
- truthful active, completed, failed, cancelled, expired, and denied frontend states supplied by the published Data Exchange projection.

deduplication, localized immutable copy, preferences and optional external
delivery. Use it only for durable user-impacting events with resolvable users;
validation errors, logs and operator incidents stay with their owning module.

Prefer built-in events from Workflow, Scheduler, Integration, batch and Report
owners. A project-owned Handler declares only the event type it may dispatch;
it does not render copy, choose arbitrary URLs or create an Inbox table.

Select the `notifications` topic in the one reading-plan request and consume
its inlined `notification.delivery_governance` machine contract before
authoring project event types or delivery rules. Consume the inlined
`notification.templates` contract only when the accepted requirement includes
an external delivery template. Do not issue separate per-category capability
calls; `notification` is the module key, not a selectable category key.
